clue.text: Stir cooked rice endlessly for Keith to eat and get 23

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so the letters around it are mixed up
endlessly says the word rice loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before the trim

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a pan of rice for Keith's supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RICE to RIC; STIR + RIC + KEITH are then rearranged by 'cooked'. 23 is FINANCE: to strike it rich is to come into money.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking it rich means suddenly gaining wealth, i.e. getting money in plenty.

clue.text: Achieve the highest place, a new peak, in a high building

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the building

parts.note: a tower is a tall building

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the word peak

explanation.surface: A climber reaches a summit by climbing a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for the peak, and 'in' places the result after the first letter of the building. 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To take power is to gain control, reaching the top position in a state or body.

clue.text: Take in the meaning?

definitions.meaning: bring goods into a country from abroad
significance, as in the purport of a remark

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a verb for bringing in goods and as a noun for significance.

clue.text: Simple addition in the cinema

parts.note: simple means easy
a rider is a clause added to a document or verdict

explanation.surface: A straightforward sum shown on the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a film title found in the cinema, the 1969 road movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is a famous 1969 film, so something to be seen at the movies.

clue.text: Single chariman ate beginning of grub to its end

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: ate means the chairman takes the letter into himself

parts.note: Mao was Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (the clue misprints chairman)

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of grub is used

explanation.surface: A lone chairman eats a grub from head to tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its end' points back to the grub: the imago is the adult, final stage of an insect's life.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the fully developed adult insect, the last stage after larva or grub.

clue.text: Criticise a large 12 for greed

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply
12 is TOWN, and a large town is a city

explanation.surface: A complaint that a big town is greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is aggressive greed, grasping desire for gain.

clue.text: Producers of music paper, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for paper is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Sheets of music paper that seem to make a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of singers, who make music.

clue.text: Parrots from part of Pakistan in steep reverse

indicators.note: reverse says the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the first bit of Pakistan inside the word for steep

parts.note: to steep is to soak

indicators.note: part of picks a run of letters from the start of Pakistan

explanation.surface: Birds from a region of Pakistan seen on a sharp slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for a slope; it is the verb. 'in' builds the container and 'reverse' turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kakapos are large flightless parrots of New Zealand.

clue.text: Sanction a covering for two pianos?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft; two of them make PP
a roof is a covering

explanation.surface: Permission sought to put a lid over a pair of pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: Approof is an old word for approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Approof is an archaic noun for approval or sanction.

clue.text: Ruler (Conservative) with £1 note to work for piano and orchestra

parts.note: an emperor is a ruler
a oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note

explanation.surface: A Tory monarch puts a pound note to use.
explanation.walkthrough: A ONCER is dated British slang for a £1 note.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto is known as the Emperor, a work for piano and orchestra.

clue.text: Place that won't change?

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the letters of the word before it

explanation.surface: A settlement that resists any alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't change' reads as stubbornness; it instructs a rearrangement of WONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a populated place.

clue.text: Publicity for mere mortals takes time and acclimatisation

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
mere means just, as in only
men are mortals

explanation.surface: Advertising for ordinary people needs time to get used to.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjustment is the process of adapting to new conditions, like acclimatisation.

clue.text: Take cover from sun's heat here

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Advice to shelter from the sun's heat in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take cover' reads as 'shelter'; it means remove the cover, as from a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe is to draw a blade from its scabbard, taking its cover off.

clue.text: Cautions for a Navy pilot's achievement going around

indicators.note: going around says the pilot's award surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a pilot earns wings on qualifying
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval pilot's badge earns warnings as he flies about.
explanation.definitionFit: Warnings and cautions are both advisories against danger.

clue.text: Get 23 for the Listener: backing can suffer from neglect

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: backing says the word can is read backwards

parts.note: metal left neglected will rust

explanation.surface: A tin left untended goes rusty while someone listens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Listener' looks like the magazine; it is just an EAR. 23 is FINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn a crust is to make a living, gaining money to live on.

Wine for a writer in the churchyard

definitions.meaning: a red or white wine of Bordeaux
Robert ... the poet, punning on the burial places in a churchyard

parts.note: the computer that draws British Premium Bond numbers shares its name with a comic of a famous double act

clue.text: Poem about the cinema

parts.note: an ode is a poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Verses written on the subject of film-going.
explanation.walkthrough: ODEON is a British chain of cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: An Odeon is a cinema, from the British chain of that name.

clue.text: Indefinite number held by fellow engaged in economics

indicators.note: held by says the number goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a fiance is a man engaged to be married
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An engaged man with a vague figure working in economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is the management of money, a branch of economics.

clue.text: Modern composer or misspelt veteran (the one in the pub?)

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of veteran are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A composer's name looks like a misspelling of veteran, or of a pub-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: John Tavener was a British composer; 'the one in the pub' plays on taverner, a tavern keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tavener was a modern English composer.

clue.text: Add salt to salt, lad for such as …

parts.note: the salt is old slang for the sea
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A cook seasons a boy's dinner with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as …' runs into the next clue: EASTER is a season.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to add salt or other flavouring.

clue.text: … cooked eats for the Queen

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of eats are mixed up

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 'such as' in the previous clue: the definition is a season.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a festival period of the church year, one of its seasons.
